clue.text: Advocates breaking into stolen capital

indicators.note: the advocates force their way inside the word for stolen goods, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
the Bar is the body of barristers, the advocates of the English courts

explanation.surface: Lawyers burgling a stash of stolen loot in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: HOBART is the capital of Tasmania, the Australian island state.
explanation.definitionFit: A state capital: the seat of government of Tasmania.

clue.text: It's divine embracing girl in time off

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first piece wraps around the girl's name

parts.note: something divine is holy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Something sacred hugging a girl while on a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacation is a spell away from work.

clue.text: Ideal material for a plinth?

parts.note: a plinth is a base, so the joke is that a metal suited to it would be named for bases; in fact the phrase means a common non-precious metal

explanation.definitionFit: Lead, zinc or copper, as opposed to gold or silver, are commonly called by this term.

clue.text: Rules the singer breaks

indicators.note: breaking the word apart and reassembling it signals a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Governing principles that a vocalist violates.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who rules is said to hold the throne, i.e. to be on it.

clue.text: Found insurance for counterpane

parts.note: to bed something is to set it down firmly, to found or embed it
cover is the protection an insurance policy gives

explanation.surface: Discovering a policy that pays out on a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpane is a bedspread laid over the top of a made-up bed.

clue.text: Aged? By jove, it might be!

indicators.note: the letters of the first word might become the answer when shuffled, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An old person exclaiming in surprise at their own age.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of surprise, mild oaths.

clue.text: Chaperon needed going round place with a rough reputation

indicators.note: the letters travel round into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A minder is required when touring a dodgy neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: CAPE HORN is the southern tip of South America, notorious for stormy seas; 'rough' refers to the waters, not the residents.
explanation.definitionFit: This headland is famed among sailors for violent weather and dangerous seas.

clue.text: It creeps through after six

indicators.note: the word for through is placed after the Roman numeral in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
per means through or by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Something sneaks in once it's past six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a creature that slithers along the ground.

clue.text: Settled for having the team in scarlet

indicators.note: the team is placed inside the colour word, signalled by the plain container word

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Footballers in red shirts having made their home somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To have settled somewhere is to have lived or dwelt there.

clue.text: One girl that is led by another

indicators.note: the abbreviation follows behind, being led by the other girl, so it comes second

parts.note: another girl, a lass
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: One young woman following another in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows 'girl' from the definition: one girl is led by another girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern English word for a young woman.

clue.text: Smoker in trousers providing music

indicators.note: the smoker is placed inside the trousers, as the container word says

parts.note: bags is old slang for loose trousers, as in Oxford bags
a pipe is what a smoker puffs

explanation.surface: A pipe-smoker in baggy trousers striking up a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for the instrument by what it gives: 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish instrument stands for the tunes it plays, by metonymy.

clue.text: Query in another form

indicators.note: putting the letters into a different shape signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question expressed in different words.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquiry is a question, and the clue's letters reshaped give this very word.

clue.text: Not a mind prepared to be masterful

indicators.note: the letters are made up afresh, like a dish prepared, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone with no brain prepared to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanding and controlling: both describe someone who takes charge.

clue.text: Her sad confusion isn't her's alone

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A muddled sad woman realising something belongs to others too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in common belongs to more than one person.

clue.text: He cuts inside the fold

parts.note: a fold is a sheep pen, so the man doing the cutting is clipping fleeces rather than paper

explanation.definitionFit: A sheep clipper removes the wool from sheep penned together.

clue.text: Still one doubts in its existence

parts.note: still means yet, as in still to come
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone who still remains sceptical about whether a thing exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'one': the creature is a thing whose existence one doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a legendary Himalayan beast many think a myth.

clue.text: Revised share-out I'd sanctioned

indicators.note: a revised version is altered, signalling that the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A reworked division of spoils was approved by me.
explanation.definitionFit: Officially approved or permitted.

clue.text: Is prone to produce a matter of contention

indicators.note: the letters are worked to produce something new, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to stir up an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy subject that causes arguments.

clue.text: Assigns to a berth in stormy seas

indicators.note: the berth goes inside the stirred-up sea letters, as the container word says
stormy seas are churned up, signalling that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a crib is a bed, a berth

explanation.surface: Allotting a sailor a bunk during rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assigns to' is the definition's verb with its usual preposition; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to someone, or allot it.

clue.text: Warmer, in the main

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and the thing that warms is an ocean current, not a general description

explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic current carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico towards Europe.

clue.text: A beggar sorting out con tents of bins

indicators.note: the letters are sorted out into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A tramp rummaging through what's in the dustbins.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is what ends up thrown away in a dustbin.

clue.text: A way through on foot

definitions.meaning: an archway, a curved opening one can pass through
the curved underside of the foot between heel and toes

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a curved, bridging shape: a passageway and part of the sole.

clue.text: Woodcutter is buried in peace

definitions.meaning: a small axe used for chopping wood
the idiom of burying an axe means making peace after a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: A small axe, and the one buried in the idiom about ending a feud.

clue.text: A jolly girl for the fleet

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman goes off to join the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish ARMADA was the fleet sent against England in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: A large naval force of warships.

clue.text: Best time to register

definitions.meaning: the fastest ever achieved in an event, a personal or world best
to note down or log formally

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a best-ever performance and a verb for writing something down.

clue.text: Material displayed by sales man in church

indicators.note: the salesman is placed inside the church abbreviation, as the container word says

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Fabric shown off by a travelling salesman during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crinkled fabric.

clue.text: Pet cried out, on its last legs

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An ailing animal whimpered, close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and close to collapse from age or neglect.

clue.text: Turn crazy in shock

indicators.note: to turn the word round is to read it from the other end

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Going mad from the trauma.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or stupefy, as a sudden blow does.

clue.text: Put out an account with wrong rebate

parts.note: AC or a/c abbreviates account

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, out of their proper order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Annoyed by a bill showing an incorrect refund.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate or embitter, to make someone irritated.

clue.text: Describing Hamlet and his rotten state

definitions.text: Describing Hamlet and his rotten state

parts.words: Describing Hamlet and his rotten state
parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, and in the play something is rotten in the state of Denmark, so the word is an adjective of nationality

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the Scandinavian kingdom where Shakespeare set the play.

clue.text: Regular lay preachers take this

parts.note: even means regular, steady
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers who preach lead the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' poses as unordained church members; it is the poetic noun for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer service, led by clergy.

clue.text: A good man in the mine, but no longer in his prime

indicators.note: the good man is placed inside the mine, as the container word says

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ST, saint, is a crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: A worthy miner underground, now ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Too old to perform as well as before.
